output.question: What is Beyond Meat's short interest?
output.answer: The latest exchange-reported figure is for October 15, 2026, from FINRA data. About 6.2 million Beyond Meat (BYND) shares were sold short, which is 36.20% of shares outstanding, with 6.86 days to cover (ShortInterestTracker). StockAnalysis, last updated November 11, 2026, shows similar numbers: 6.22M shares short, up from 5.70M the month before. That works out to 34.02% of shares outstanding and 39.96% of float, with a short ratio of 4.93 days. Share counts are small because Beyond Meat did a 1-for-30 reverse stock split on August 14, 2026, and short interest has stayed around 34–40% of shares.

key_facts.fact: FINRA reported 6.2M BYND shares sold short as of October 15, 2026. That is 36.20% of shares outstanding, with 6.86 days to cover.
StockAnalysis shows short interest of 6.22M shares, up from 5.70M the previous month. That is 34.02% of shares outstanding and 39.96% of float, with a short ratio of 4.93.
Beyond Meat carried out a 1-for-30 reverse stock split, and split-adjusted trading began August 14, 2026. This is why the share counts are low.

passages.quote: The latest short interest is 6.22 million, so 34.02% of the outstanding shares have been sold short.

caveats: The sources disagree on percentages (34.02%, 36.20%, 39.96%) because they divide by different bases (shares outstanding vs. float) and may use different share counts.
Days to cover differs between sources (6.86 vs. 4.93) because each uses a different average-volume window.
The October 15, 2026 FINRA figure may already have been replaced by the late-October settlement data (normally published in early November), which I could not confirm.
A search snippet attributed a 38.5%-of-free-float estimate and a 28.82% cost to borrow to ORTEX as of October 21, 2026. I could not open that page, so those numbers are not verified.
I could not open the MarketBeat, Benzinga and GuruFocus pages (HTTP 403).
